title: USAir 5050
summary: During takeoff from LaGuardia runway 31 on a wet runway in darkness and low visibility, the aircraft drifted to the left. The captain's improper use of the nosewheel steering tiller damaged the left nose tire, and a loud bang followed. The captain aborted the takeoff but was unable to stop the aircraft before it ran off the runway end into Bowery Bay, breaking into three fuselage sections.
probable_cause: The captain's failure to exercise command authority to reject the takeoff or take sufficient control to continue it, which was initiated with a mistrimmed rudder. Also causal was failure to detect the mistrimmed rudder before takeoff (p. 57).

factors.evidence: Failure of crew to detect improper rudder trim setting despite checklists during pre-flight procedures; captain failed to detect mistrimmed rudder before takeoff was attempted (p. 55-57).

Captain failed to provide extended briefing or emergency briefing and crew had coordination problems transferring control during takeoff roll; poor communication between captain and first officer (p. 38-42).
Failure to detect improper rudder trim setting by means of rudder pedal displacement during taxiing; rudder trim control not checked as part of cross-check procedures (p. 40).

As the first officer began the takeoff on runway 31, the airplane started to drift to the left; captain attempted to correct that drift with improper nosewheel steering tiller use, damaging left nose tire (p. 9).
Weather conditions included darkness, low visibility and wet runway during takeoff; flight was part of extra section decision made just before boarding causing time pressure (p. 8-10).

Aircraft was unable to stop before running off end of runway into Bowery Bay; fuselage broke into three sections with forward section resting on elevated light stanchion and aft section partially submerged (p. 9).

events.text: Captain and first officer report to USAir operations at BWI to fly B-737 N416US to LaGuardia as Flight 1846; scheduled departure 1510 but delayed to 1935 due to LGA inbound air traffic
Flight 1846 arrives at LaGuardia Gate 15 after leaving BWI uneventfully; dispatcher cancels Norfolk leg and later reassigns aircraft to operate as Flight 5050 to Charlotte with passengers
Passengers board Flight 5050; captain visits USAir ground movement control tower expressing concern about crew duty time limitations before end of trip
As first officer began takeoff on runway 31, airplane drifted to the left due to mistrimmed rudder; captain attempted to correct drift using nosewheel steering tiller
Flightcrew heard loud bang followed by continuous rumbling noise; left nose tire damaged by improper tiller use
Captain took over control from first officer and rejected takeoff by aborting
Captain unable to stop airplane before it ran off end of runway into Bowery Bay
Fuselage broke into three sections; forward section rested on part of elevated light stanchion; aft section partially submerged in Bowery Bay

recommendations.text: Require an operational rule that, during takeoff roll, should an uncommanded deviation from the intended flight path occur, the pilot-not-flying shall explicitly advise the pilot-flying of the deviation and the pilot-flying shall acknowledge the deviation; if the deviation persists or another uncommanded deviation occurs, either pilot shall be authorized to execute a rejected takeoff without coordination.

Require a revision of the pre-takeoff instrument procedures and flight crew handbook requirements so that they address positional sensing of controls that are not normally visible to either pilot during the normal scan.
Require cockpit resource management (CRM) training for all U.S. air carriers, including those not currently required to provide formal CRM training.
Require pre-takeoff briefings for rejected takeoff procedures in all U.S. carrier flight training departments.

Require a comprehensive study by aircraft manufacturers of rudder trim control design and placement to determine how the systems can be designed to provide more positive feedback of control position to flightcrews.
Require that all runway safety areas meet the recommendations contained in the 1988 FAA Advisory Circular AC 150/5300-13.

Require aircraft manufacturers to make a comprehensive analysis of the problem of water ingestion during overwater emergency landings and to publish design guidance that will improve aircrew survivability in such events.
Require improved testing of aircraft emergency evacuation procedures with emphasis on the effectiveness of emergency exits and evacuation aids under adverse environmental conditions.
Require a comprehensive study of postaccident aircrew availability to determine the optimum method for obtaining postaccident statements from aircrew.
